description: Dull olive, pale flat eyes, a gape wider than the skull carrying it. One bite. Rarely two.
lore: The Chronicle files this one beside the burning one because at forty paces they have the same silhouette, and there the resemblance stops. Nothing about this animal is on fire. It is the colour of lichen on a north face, dull olive going grey, mottled so finely that if it holds still against wet stone there is nothing there to see. The eyes are the wrong colour for eyes, flat and pale and pinkish at the inner corner, and it fell out of a life spent in water under stone, in the dark, where they cannot have been much use to it either. What it did bring down with it was the jaw. The head is most of the creature and the jaw is most of the head, hinged much further back than looks reasonable, so that the gape comes out wider than the skull carrying it. One bite, delivered without any preamble at all, and generally that is the encounter.

What it does now is take the hard things. Bone first: it will spend an entire night on a single marrow bone and leave it knobbed, stained and lying in the open, which is how anyone knows one is working an area. Bone is only where it starts. Stone gets chewed; what cannot be chewed gets swallowed; and of everything on that mountain that will not soften or wear or go anywhere, the best by a long way is gold, which it takes whenever it finds any, though not one of these creatures has ever been opened up with gold still inside it. There is no mystery in the appetite once you have watched this country for a season. Everything else goes. A hillside goes, a path goes, a fat reliable thing you were counting on goes soft where it stands and then is not anywhere at all. A creature that will only take what refuses to go is, in its blunt way, the most sensible thing on that mountain, and it has never at any point known that about itself. It works ground that other things have quietly stopped working, nearer the cave than anything out there that still has an inside.

The paws it sheds are never a matching pair: three pale curled claws on a scrap of mottled hide, and the next one off the same animal is subtly the wrong shape. Whatever grows back after a loss comes back approximate, and the one after that comes back approximate from the approximation. The hard piece prised out of the jaw carries that whole history in a single object, sea-green and broken clean through, the break filled in with gold. The mend gets explained two ways and both ways have people who will swear by them: that the gold is everything hard the creature ever took, gone at last to the one part of it that could hold anything; or that the crack came first and the gold went in after, and the appetite was only ever the animal trying to get back what it had already lost. Worked into armour it makes the armour hold, and carried about it seems to arrange for gold to turn up.
